kinds.description: The single source-of-truth map of src/'s module boundaries and responsibilities. A stale citation here usually means that module's real responsibility shifted — re-read the section and confirm it still describes what the file actually does, don't just re-stamp the hash.

The package's own index, linking every sibling doc. A stale citation to a sibling usually means that doc was restructured — confirm the link still points at the right section, not just that the file still exists.

States why this work matters, grounded in a cited spike (see this package's grounded_by rule). If that spike changed, re-check whether it still supports the stated need — a changed spike can quietly invalidate the whole problem statement.

Ranks directions against a cited spike's evidence. If that spike changed, re-check whether the ranking or a rejected option's reasoning still holds — a stale citation here can mean a decision now rests on outdated evidence.

Real, run feasibility evidence, not narrated. If the code this spike cites changed, the primitive it once confirmed working may no longer be — don't assume it still is; re-run the spike or downgrade the citing doc's confidence.
Maps the real user workflow to a walking-skeleton release scope. If a cited doc changed, check whether the walking skeleton it marks out is still accurately described.
Sequences shippable releases, grounded in a cited spike and derived from a cited story-map. A stale citation to either means the sequencing rationale may need re-justifying, not just re-stamping.

Concrete enough to implement from directly, built on a cited spike's validated primitive (see this package's builds_on rule). If that spike changed, confirm the primitive is still validated before trusting this doc's approach.

Reusable lessons, sourced from a cited spike. If that spike changed, re-verify the lesson still accurately reflects it — a lesson can quietly go stale even when the underlying technique is still fine.
